specialist_assessments.assessment: Source observations: the five routes are separate HTML documents. Each loads the shared `src/app.js`, and four also load a route-specific module. The shared code is limited to helpers such as toast rendering; route markup and most displayed metrics are authored directly in each HTML file. Orders renders from the fixed `orders` array, while the customer route contains its cards in HTML and its module imports but does not use the `customers` array. The analytics slider updates its label and a fixed two-value count. Inference: this is a small, low-overhead static fixture, but several route interactions are demonstrations rather than data-backed operations. No project code, scripts, tests, builds, or servers were run. There are no attached screenshots, so rendered behavior and visual appearance are not assessed, and no performance measurements are available.

evidence.description: The overview loads the shared app module after its static page markup.
The orders route loads the shared app module and a route-specific orders module.

Customer records are embedded as static cards in the route markup.
The included test source covers fixture presence and currency formatting only; it does not cover route interactions.

specialist_assessments.assessment: Source-only assessment: the five routes use native links for navigation and route-specific JavaScript for local search, filters, a record dialog, settings controls, and toast feedback. The toast and settings save status use live-region semantics. The reviewed handlers contain no request lifecycle; the settings form has a delayed simulated failure. Material interaction gaps include off-screen mobile navigation remaining focusable, incomplete modal focus handling, inert directory and order controls, and feedback that can disagree with the resulting settings state. No rendered appearance or live keyboard, touch, or runtime behavior was verified.

specialist_assessments.assessment: The overview has a consistent operations-dashboard visual identity across the three supplied viewports. Desktop clearly separates navigation, KPIs, revenue/activity panels, and operational summaries. Tablet and mobile retain the same hierarchy while moving navigation into a compact header and reflowing the content. No clear visual failure is evident in the supplied images. One optional mobile refinement is to reduce how much of the first viewport the stacked KPI cards occupy; this is a scroll-depth tradeoff, not evidence of clipping or missing content.

evidence.description: At 1440×1000, the dark navigation rail and white top bar frame a clear sequence: greeting and actions, four KPIs in one row, then revenue and activity panels, followed by fulfillment and notes. Source corroboration: index.html:7 contains the dashboard sections; assets/styles.css:2 defines the base layout and card styling.

At 768×1024, navigation is represented by a menu icon in the top bar, KPIs reflow into a 2×2 grid, and the revenue panel spans the content width. The recent activity panel begins below it. Source corroboration: assets/styles.css:7-8 defines the grid and compact-header breakpoints.

At 390×844, the header remains compact, the two actions share a row, and KPI cards stack vertically. The viewport ends partway through the fourth KPI card; this shows the viewport boundary, not that the card or later content is clipped in the page. Source corroboration: assets/styles.css:9 defines the single-column mobile KPI and content layout.

specialist_assessments.assessment: Pass 2 confirms the restrained operations-dashboard identity and the described desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts for route /. One appearance claim needs correction: the mobile primary action is teal, not dark. Source observation: index.html:7 orders the four metric cards before the later dashboard panels; assets/styles.css:7-9 reflows the metrics from four columns to two and then one column, and puts the content panels in a single column at the supplied tablet and mobile widths. Rendered observation: the mobile screenshot shows the first three KPI cards fully and the fourth partly within the 390×844 capture; the trend and activity panels are not visible there. Inference: reaching those panels requires scrolling past the KPI stack. That is a low-priority information-density tradeoff, not evidence of clipping or lost content. Measurements: viewport dimensions are those supplied in the evidence inventory; no new pixel measurements were made. Hypothesis: a denser mobile KPI presentation could expose trends sooner, with less room around each metric.

specialist_assessments.assessment: The /analytics/ desktop view has a clear dashboard hierarchy: persistent navigation, a prominent page heading and download action, two data panels, then the order explorer. Its navy, cool gray, white, and teal palette and compact sans-serif typography feel consistent across the supplied renders. The responsive layouts have a visible horizontal overflow issue: at tablet width the acquisition panel is pushed past the right edge, and at mobile width the chart panel extends beyond the viewport. The captures do not establish whether horizontal scrolling is available.

specialist_assessments.assessment: The candidate assessment is mostly supported, with one clarification: at tablet width the acquisition panel is not wholly absent; a narrow slice of its left edge is visible, while its contents are clipped beyond the right edge. The desktop view shows the full dashboard hierarchy and both analytics panels. At mobile width, the chart card extends beyond the right edge; only the Direct and Retail categories are visible in the supplied capture, and the acquisition panel is also only partly shown. Source observation: `analytics/index.html:7` places both panels in `.layout-2`; `assets/styles.css:2` defines the two-column grid, `assets/styles.css:4` sets `.analytics-page .chart-frame` to `min-width:680px`, and the one-column `.layout-2` rule appears at `assets/styles.css:9` (the 520px breakpoint). Inference: the chart minimum width contributes to horizontal overflow, while the two-column layout remains active at the 768px tablet viewport. The supplied screenshots do not establish how horizontal scrolling behaves.

specialist_assessments.assessment: The /customers/ page has a clear, restrained SaaS directory design: a pale cool-gray canvas, dark slate text and navigation, teal primary action, and white customer cards. The title and short eyebrow establish the page hierarchy, while names, avatars, locations, and two customer metrics are grouped consistently. The layout adapts from three card columns on desktop to two on tablet and one on mobile; the search and filters also stack on mobile. Two visible refinements are warranted: the second card has noticeably sharper corners than its peers, and the desktop sidebar footer initials are faint against their avatar background.

Interactions and states beyond the supplied default screenshots were not assessed.
